TITLE: Lightweight Pruning with Quantitative Analysis of Importance Metrics
PROPOSAL: We experiment with pruning-based lightweight methods, critically comparing the efficiency-robustness trade-off of several importance metrics including magnitude, entropy, and GCN-based attention metrics. We also apply a novel saliency-guided pruning strategy, leveraging saliency maps as an iterative importance metric, to balance sparsity and retain crucial features. Our goal is to establish a quantitative analysis of the relationship between pruning metric selection, model efficiency, and segmentation performance on real-world clinical datasets.
CONTROLS: Baselines will be a comprehensive set of pruning schemes unavailable at our knowledge cutoff with various sparsity schedules, including hand-tuned, example-wise and automatic pruning; an ablation of individual importance metrics for GCN-based attention to study their relative impact on efficiency and robustness; and a simple unpruned network with 30M parameters for benchmarking. We also compare our pruned network against mid-sized 3D models from recent literature (e.g., those in Chapter 3).
COST: 100 GPU-hours (including retraining and pruning multiple architectures)
PREDICTION: Our analysis will reveal the most effective pruning strategy (chosen by validation accuracy and convergence speed), while providing a method to estimate pruning's trade-off schemes in the future. However, our pruning method may not outperform large, state-of-the-art 3D models or lack generalizability, highlighting the potential for future work on meta-pruning strategies.

TITLE: Hybrid Real-World and Synthetic Pet/CT Tumor Segmentation Dataset Creation
PROPOSAL: To mitigate the difficulties associated with dataset scarcity and class imbalanced samples in whole-body 3D PET/CT tumor segmentation, we propose combining the advances in medical simulation tools to synthesize medical images from clinical templates with real-world data leveraging data augmentation and  virtual scan creation. Utilizing Atlas-based models of organs of interest, we simulate tumor growth of various types (e.g., breast, prostate, lung) in synthetic PET/CT volumes. 
CONTROLS: Performance metrics for ablation studies will include lossless image copying, Hounsfield unit discrepancy, and variance-based quality assessment. Baseline tested on our real-world/synthetic dataset will be the FLAIR atlas used for clickable voxel scan editions of lesions in typical open dataset space case.
COST: 50 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: Our datasets will significantly improve real-world and synthetic tumor likelihood, greatly facilitate medical segmentation research team diversity and mitigate a major problem for decision-wise virtual analysis — namely simulating rare cancer cases.

TITLE: Transferring Reconstruction Knowledge to Improve 3D Medical Segmentation
PROPOSAL: To overcome the regions-of-interest mismatch between reconstruction and segmentation tasks, we propose a novel reconstruction-aided segmentation (RAS) framework that leverages detail learned from unlabeled data by a reconstruction task to guide the segmentation network. The RAS framework integrates a multi-task supervised learning approach, where the segmentation network is trained alongside a reconstruction network that learns to reconstruct unlabeled images. This cross-task transfer enables the segmentation network to benefit from the reconstruction network's learning of object details and geometry.
CONTROLS: Performance comparisons will be made with: (1) the original segmentation network without RAS; (2) a segmentation network with a pre-trained reconstruction encoder; and (3) a baseline segmentation network trained on the same dataset without RAS. We also investigate the effectiveness of RAS in various reconstruction-synthesized data transfer scenarios.
COST: 120 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: Our RAS framework will lead to significant improvements in segmentation accuracy and robustness, especially for complex anatomical structures and lesions, by leveraging the reconstruction network's learning of detailed object features. However, the effectiveness of our approach may depend on the specific reconstruction network architecture and training process used, and potential issues with overfitting to the reconstruction task may arise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multimodal Fusion with Attention-based Early Fusion and Late Fusion for Lightweight 3D Segmentation
PROPOSAL: To effectively exploit complementary information from multiple imaging modalities, we propose a lightweight multimodal fusion framework that combines attention-based early fusion and late fusion strategies. Our approach uses modality-transformers to selectively weigh input features from different modalities and encode their relationships, followed by a attention-guided late fusion aggregation to pool features from multiple modalities. We also explore variant early fusion approaches to reduce computational costs.
CONTROLS: Performance comparisons will be made with: (1) a lightweight segmentation network trained on a single modality; (2) a segmentation network with a mid-sized multimodal fusion component; and (3) a baseline segmentation network without multimodal fusion. We analyze the impact of early fusion strategies on model efficiency and robustness.
COST: 150 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: Our multimodal fusion framework will demonstrate improved segmentation accuracy and robustness across heterogeneous modalities, especially for complex anatomical structures and lesions. However, the effective utilization of modality-transformers may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and may not scale well with the number of modalities.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: 2. Transferring Reconstruction Knowledge to Improve 3D Medical Segmentation
PROPOSAL: To enhance the transfer learning capability of our reconstruction-aided segmentation (RAS) framework, we incorporate a meta-learning approach to adapt the RAS to new organ-specific tasks. We pre-train the RAS on a set of synthetic or subset real-world images to learn a task-agnostic representation. Then, we meta-train the RAS using a learning-to-learn approach to adapt the pre-trained RAS to new tasks, such as new organs or lesion types, with a few example images. This adaptability is essential for real-world clinical applications where new organs or lesions need to be segmented.
CONTROLS: Performance comparisons will be made with: (1) the original RAS framework without meta-learning; (2) a meta-trained RAS with fixed task-agnostic representations; and (3) a segmentation network with separate adaptation for each task. We also investigate the transferability of learned task-agnostic representations between tasks.
COST: 80 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: Our meta-learning approach will significantly enhance the RAS framework's adaptability to new tasks, enabling real-world clinical applications with diverse organs and lesion types. However, the effectiveness of our approach may depend on the quality of the pre-training dataset and the meta-training process, which could be challenging to optimize.

TITLE: Efficient 3D Segmentation using RWKV and Mamba with Optimal Scanning Strategies
PROPOSAL: To address the challenges of real-world clinical data and heterogeneous lesions, we combine the strengths of RWKV and Mamba sequence models with optimal scanning strategies. RWKV is used for its linear memory requirement and efficient attention mechanism, while Mamba is employed for its flexibility in modeling long-range dependencies. We also propose a novel scanning strategy to effectively explore the 3D volume, reducing redundant computations and improving segmentation accuracy.
CONTROLS: Performance comparisons will be made with: (1) standard RWKV and Mamba models; (2) RWKV and Mamba with fixed scanning strategies; and (3) a CNN-Transformer based segmentation network. We investigate the impact of scanning strategy optimization on segmentation results.
COST: 90 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: Our approach will demonstrate improved efficiency and robustness in real-world clinical segmentation tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art lightweight models. However, the effectiveness of our scanning strategy may depend on the specific RWKV and Mamba architecture, which could be challenging to optimize.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: 1. Lightweight Pruning with Quantitative Analysis of Importance Metrics
PROPOSAL: To enhance the pruning strategy, we incorporate a novel importance metric based on attention-weighted gradient upper bound (AWGUB) and assess its impact on pruning performance. AWGUB measures the sensitivity of each model weight to changes in input features, based on the attention weights and gradient values. We evaluate its effectiveness in pruning networks with varying complexities and compare it with existing importance metrics.
CONTROLS: Performance comparisons will be made with: (1) the original pruning framework with magnitude importance metric; (2) AWGUB with different pruning sparsity levels; and (3) an ablation study to analyze the impact of each component on pruning performance.
COST: 60 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: Our AWGUB-based pruning metric will demonstrate improved efficiency and robustness in pruning networks, leading to better trade-offs between model complexity and pruning sparsity. However, the effectiveness of AWGUB may depend on the specific pruning algorithm and network architecture, which could be challenging to optimize.

TITLE: 4. Efficient 3D Segmentation using RWKV and Mamba with Optimal Scanning Strategies
PROPOSAL: To further improve the efficiency of RWKV-MAMBA segmentation, we propose a dynamic scheduling mechanism to adaptively allocate computational resources between RWKV and MAMBA blocks based on their respective computational demands and segmentation accuracy requirements. This adaptive scheduling strategy will enable RWKV-MAMBA to efficiently handle various complexities of 3D medical images while maintaining high accuracy.
CONTROLS: Performance comparisons will be made with: (1) the original RWKV-MAMBA model without adaptive scheduling; (2) RWKV-MAMBA with static scheduling; and (3) a CNN-Transformer based segmentation network with adaptive resource allocation. We also analyze the impact of scheduling strategy on segmentation results.
COST: 70 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: Our adaptive scheduling mechanism will significantly improve the efficiency and robustness of RWKV-MAMBA segmentation, leading to better trade-offs between accuracy and computational resources. However, the effectiveness of our approach may depend on the specific RWKV-MAMBA architecture and scheduling strategy, which could be challenging to optimize.

TITLE: Large-Scale Evaluation and Deployment of Lightweight 3D Segmentation Models
PROPOSAL: To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed lightweight 3D segmentation models in real-world clinical settings, we plan to conduct a large-scale evaluation on several comprehensive 3D medical benchmark datasets, including the Head-Neck Tumor Segmentation Challenge (HNTSC) and the Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) challenge. Additionally, we propose to develop a user-friendly deployment framework for integrating our models into clinical workflows, enabling seamless integration of lightweight 3D segmentation models into medical diagnostic pipelines.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our models against state-of-the-art models on HNTSC and BraTS challenges and engage with clinical experts to prototype our deployment framework.
COST: 100 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: This evaluation will provide a comprehensive assessment of our lightweight models' performance in real-world scenarios and offer valuable insights into their strengths and limitations. The deployment framework will facilitate the adoption of our models in clinical settings, promoting widespread use and improving patient care.

TITLE: Efficient Transformers for Lightweight 3D Medical Image Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Design and train a lightweight variant of theNeoFormer model, a state-of-the-art 3D transformer architecture, with a parameter count under 3 million. Apply a combination of kernel pruning and factorized attention to significantly reduce computational complexity and memory requirements. Evaluate its performance on whole-body PET/CT tumor lesion segmentation and head and neck tumor segmentation in PET/CT datasets, comparing it to standard NeoFormer and other lightweight 3D segmentation models like UNET++ and 3D-UNet.
CONTROLS: Standard NeoFormer with PyTorch default settings, UNET++ with 3D convolutions
COST: 200 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The lightweight NeoFormer variant should match the performance of standard NeoFormer on smaller organs and lesions, with a 2x reduction in computations and memory usage, but may struggle with larger lesions and more complex anatomies where standard NeoFormer excels. 

Its performance may also be negatively impacted by the pruning which could make it harder to focus on relevant features and affect the network's ability to capture the hierarchical correlations presented in 3D scans. 

The benefits of said pruning could still prevail over its limitations, allowing it to prevail in experiments with multiple organs and anatomies relative to typical neural network variants.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Multimodal Fusion for Lightweight 3D Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of lightweight fourier transform (LWT) for multimodal fusion in 3D medical image segmentation. Specifically, apply LWT to combine features from MRI and PET/CT modalities, enabling efficient feature sharing and fusion without increasing computational complexity. Integrate this with the lightweight NeoFormer variant proposed in experiment 1, and evaluate its performance on brain tumor segmentation in multi-sequence MRI and whole-body PET/CT tumor lesion segmentation datasets, comparing the results to those achieved with standard NeoFormer and other fusion methods like channel-wise attention.
CONTROLS: Standard NeoFormer with PyTorch default settings, standard NeoFormer with channel-wise attention
COST: 150 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The use of LWT for multimodal fusion should allow efficient sharing of features between MRI and PET/CT modalities, leading to improved performance on segmentation tasks with combined data, while the lightweight NeoFormer variant's reduced complexity will minimize computations spent during the process, suggesting an overall significant performance boost in comparison to standard NeoFormer and other fusion methods.

TITLE: Efficient Transfer of Prior Knowledge for Lightweight 3D Segmentation
REVISE: 2
PROPOSAL: Revising the second proposal, replace the use of LWT for multimodal fusion with a lightweight PyTorch implementation of the MoCo v3 model, using a within-modality pretext task to acquire robust prior knowledge about boundaries and lesion characteristics. Train MoCo v3 on a separate dataset of volumetric images and use a lightweight neural network to transfer this knowledge to the standard NeoFormer model, and then to the lightweight NeoFormer variant. Evaluate the transferred knowledge's impact on segmentation performance for brain tumor segmentation in multi-sequence MRI and whole-body PET/CT tumor lesion segmentation.
CONTROLS: Standard NeoFormer with PyTorch default settings, standard NeoFormer trained on pretext task only
COST: 250 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The acquisition and transfer of prior knowledge using MoCo v3 should enable the lightweight segmentation model to generalize better to new datasets and scenarios, leveraging the robustness of learned representations without increasing the overall computational cost. This knowledge transfer approach is also expected to better suit segmentations with complex anatomies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Scanning Strategies for Lightweight 3D Medical Image Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of adaptive hierarchical scanning strategies for lightweight 3D medical image segmentation. The proposed method would start with a coarse resolution to efficiently sample the entire 3D volume, and then progressively increase the resolution around regions identified as interesting by a lightweight neural network. This method should significantly reduce the computational cost of 3D image segmentation while maintaining or even improving segmentation accuracy. Evaluate its performance on head and neck tumor segmentation in PET/CT and whole-body PET/CT tumor lesion segmentation datasets.
CONTROLS: UNET++ with 3D convolutions and adaptive hierarchical scanning strategy
COST: 300 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The proposed adaptive hierarchical scanning strategy should significantly reduce the computational cost of 3D image segmentation while maintaining or even improving segmentation accuracy, leading to faster and more efficient segmentation of medical images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lightweight 3D Segmentation with Low-Rank Attention
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of low-rank attention mechanisms in lightweight 3D medical image segmentation models. Specifically, apply a low-rank matrix factorization to the attention weights in the NeoFormer model, reducing its dimensionality and portioning the complexity in smaller, more manageable parts. Evaluate the low-rank NeoFormer variant's performance on whole-body PET/CT tumor lesion segmentation and head and neck tumor segmentation in PET/CT, comparing its results to the original NeoFormer and the model proposed in experiment 1.
CONTROLS: Standard NeoFormer, lightweight NeoFormer variant with adaptive hierarchical scanning strategy
COST: 180 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The adoption of low-rank attention should significantly reduce the weight matrix complexity within NeoFormer, making it both more robust and efficient for handling various types of large anatomies present in volumetric medical imaging, thus expected to match the expression-to-solution jumping capacity of NeoFormer, but at lower cost.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Comparison of Scanning Strategies for Lightweight 3D Segmentation
REVISE: 3
PROPOSAL: Revise the third proposal to directly compare the performance of different scanning strategies on lightweight 3D medical image segmentation. This includes the adaptive hierarchical scanning strategy proposed earlier, and a baseline uniform scanning strategy. Additionally, include a random sampling strategy as a control to assess the importance of adaptiveness in the scanning strategy. Evaluate all three scanning strategies on head and neck tumor segmentation in PET/CT and whole-body PET/CT tumor lesion segmentation datasets, comparing their impact on segmentation accuracy, processing time, and memory usage.
CONTROLS: UNET++ with 3D convolutions and uniform scanning strategy
COST: 220 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The adaptive hierarchical scanning strategy is expected to offer the best trade-off between segmentation accuracy, processing time, and memory usage, followed by the uniform scanning strategy, while the random sampling strategy will likely perform the worst due to inefficient sampling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablation Study of Lightweight 3D Segmentation Methods
PROPOSAL: Conduct a comprehensive ablation study to investigate the impact of individual components in the lightweight 3D segmentation methods proposed earlier. Specifically, analyze the contributions of low-rank attention, multimodal fusion, and adaptive hierarchical scanning strategy to the overall performance of the lightweight segmentation model. Compare the performance of different combinations of these components to understand their interactions and identify the most important factors for improving segmentation accuracy and efficiency.
CONTROLS: Baseline model with only pruning
COST: 250 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The results of the ablation study should shed light on the relative importance of different components in lightweight 3D segmentation methods, providing a better understanding of their interactions and optimal configurations. This will enable the identification of the most effective design choices for achieving high-performance and efficiency in lightweight 3D segmentation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Comparison of Proposed Methods on Brain Tumor Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Conduct a real-world comparison of the proposed lightweight 3D segmentation methods on brain tumor segmentation in multi-sequence MRI datasets. Evaluate the performance of the lightweight NeoFormer variant, the model with low-rank attention, the adaptive hierarchical scanning strategy, and the ablated model on publicly available datasets such as BraTS and RTOG.
CONTROLS: Standard NeoFormer, popular 3D segmentation models for brain tumor segmentation (e.g., 3D-UNet, UNET++-ResNext)
COST: 350 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The proposed lightweight 3D segmentation methods should demonstrate competitive performance to standard NeoFormer and other popular models on brain tumor segmentation, offering advantages in terms of efficiency and computational cost. However, the results may vary depending on the complexity of the tumors and the type of MRI sequences used, which could lead to challenges in segmenting complex or heterogeneous lesions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lightweight 3D Segmentation on Head and Neck Tumors with Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the application of the proposed lightweight 3D segmentation methods to head and neck tumor segmentation in PET/CT datasets. Additionally, incorporate uncertainty estimation into the model to quantify the confidence of the segmentation output. Evaluate the performance of the uncertainty estimation on various metrics (e.g., uncertainty map quality, segmentation accuracy under uncertainty).
CONTROLS: Standard NeoFormer with uncertainty estimation, popular 3D segmentation models with uncertainty estimation (e.g., 3D-UNet with MC dropout)
COST: 320 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The inclusion of uncertainty estimation in the lightweight 3D segmentation model should enable better handling of complex or uncertain anatomical structures, such as head and neck tumors, while maintaining the efficiency advantages of the proposed lightweight methods.

PROPOSAL: Scale up the proposed lightweight 3D segmentation methods to handle large-scale whole-body PET/CT datasets, which pose significant computational challenges due to their vast size and complexity. Investigate efficient ways to parallelize the computation and utilize distributed computing architectures to accelerate the segmentation process. Evaluate the performance of the lightweight segmentation model on a public dataset with a large sample size.
CONTROLS: Baseline standard NeoFormer with default settings, popular 3D segmentation models for whole-body PET/CT (e.g., 3D-UNet with large kernel)
COST: 450 GPU-hours (estimated)
PREDICTION: The application of the proposed lightweight 3D segmentation methods to large-scale whole-body PET/CT datasets should enable efficient and accurate segmentation of complex anatomical structures, such as tumors, while minimizing the computational resources required. However, the results may vary depending on the available computational resources and the complexity of the dataset, which could lead to convergence issues or inaccuracies in the segmentation output.
